subsystems.name: Identity and access management
subsystems.role: verifies who or what is making every request, continuously.

subsystems.name: AI policy engine
subsystems.role: decides in real time whether a request should be allowed, based on context and learned behaviour.

subsystems.name: Microsegmentation and enforcement
subsystems.role: divides the network into small zones and blocks lateral movement if something is compromised.

subsystems.name: Telemetry pipeline
subsystems.role: collects signals from across users, devices, workloads and networks.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and automation
subsystems.role: acts on policy decisions by changing access, isolating workloads or triggering investigations.
parts: security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) platform

buildSteps.title: Inventory assets and data flows
buildSteps.detail: Map every user, device, application and service, and record how they communicate. You cannot protect what you have not identified.

buildSteps.title: Define trust zones and policies
buildSteps.detail: Group assets by sensitivity and function, then write explicit rules for what may talk to what, under which conditions.

buildSteps.title: Deploy strong identity for users and workloads
buildSteps.detail: Enforce multi-factor authentication, issue short-lived credentials, and give every workload a verifiable identity.

buildSteps.title: Roll out microsegmentation
buildSteps.detail: Insert policy enforcement points between zones, typically using software agents or network overlays, so traffic is denied by default.

buildSteps.title: Instrument telemetry
buildSteps.detail: Stream logs, flow records and identity events into a central platform so the AI has continuous, high-quality data to learn from.

buildSteps.title: Train and validate AI models
buildSteps.detail: Use historical and simulated data to teach models normal behaviour and common attack patterns, then test them against red-team exercises.

buildSteps.title: Integrate orchestration with enforcement points
buildSteps.detail: Connect the policy engine to firewalls, identity providers and endpoint tools through APIs so decisions can be applied automatically.

buildSteps.title: Operate and continuously retrain
buildSteps.detail: Run the system in monitor-and-recommend mode first, then allow automatic enforcement as confidence grows, retraining models as the environment changes.

prerequisites.why: zero trust requires knowing exactly who or what is requesting access before any decision can be made.
without fine-grained network controls, a single breach can spread unchecked.

prerequisites.tech: AI and machine learning for security analytics
prerequisites.why: models that spot subtle anomalies in real time are still maturing and can produce false positives.
orchestration needs to talk to many different tools, but not all expose standard interfaces.
AI models are only as good as the data they learn from, so consistent logging is essential.

pathway.milestone: zero trust architecture with manual policy definition and basic automation
pathway.unlocks: a reduced attack surface and clearer audit trails.

pathway.milestone: AI-assisted policy recommendations and automated responses to common threats
pathway.unlocks: faster reaction times and less burden on security teams.

pathway.milestone: real-time autonomous policy enforcement across hybrid cloud environments
pathway.unlocks: consistent security regardless of where users or workloads are located.

pathway.milestone: self-optimising zero trust that predicts and preempts attacks
pathway.unlocks: proactive defence with minimal human intervention.
